preamble: Monophthongization of the rising diphthong [we] to [o], keeping the rounding of the glide and the mid height of the nucleus. It is lexically restricted to the Spanish discourse particle pues 'well, then', which colloquially becomes pos (Mexico and elsewhere) or, with loss of the final /s/, po (Andalusia, Murcia, Chile). It is not a general sound law of Spanish; alternations such as cuento ~ contar reflect stress-conditioned diphthongization of Latin ŏ, the reverse direction.

examples.note: Colloquial reduction of the discourse particle pues; the rising diphthong [we] coalesces into the back rounded vowel [o].
In very colloquial Murcian /ue/ in pues is monophthongized to /o/, realized open [ɔ] because the following /s/ is lost.

examples.to: po (Andalusia, Chile), as in ¡sí po! 'yes, of course!'
examples.note: Emphatic particle derived from pues, with the diphthong reduced to [o] and final /s/ lost.

sources: Monroy, R., & Hernández-Campoy, J. M. (2015). Murcian Spanish. Journal of the International Phonetic Association, 45(2), 229–240. https://doi.org/10.1017/S0025100314000231
